turkmenistan.title: Flag of Turkmenistan

colors.note: Represents Islam and the country's lush landscape
The vertical carpet-pattern stripe representing the five major Turkmen tribes
The crescent and stars above the carpet pattern

desc:
- Green field with a vertical red stripe near the hoist containing five carpet guls, a white crescent and five white stars in the upper hoist, and two crossed olive branches beneath the guls
- Adopted on 19 February 1992 and amended in 2001 to add olive branches; current proportions set in 2001

countryData.name: Turkmenistan
countryData.location: Central Asia, east of the Caspian Sea

trivia:
- Often described as the world's most complex national flag because of its intricate carpet medallions (guls)
- The five guls represent the Teke, Yomut, Saryk, Chovdur, and Ersary tribes; olive branches were added in 2001 to reflect Turkmenistan's UN-recognised permanent neutrality
- The five stars echo the country's five provinces (welayats)
